Chapter 8: Praying for Purpose, Direction, and Calling
You know, there’s a longing deep in every parent’s heart—to see their child discover real purpose. We want them to find work that matters, to live a life that means something, to know, without a doubt, that they’re making a difference.
But if you’ve ever watched a loved one try to figure it all out, you’ll know—the path to purpose is rarely a straight line. It’s full of detours, doubts, and seasons where you just feel lost.
I remember a young woman, restless in her career, who’d call her parents again and again, sharing her uncertainty. She’d wonder out loud if she’d chosen the wrong path, or if she’d ever find work that truly felt significant. Her parents listened patiently, recalling their own winding journeys. And amid all her questions, they prayed—for clarity, for new doors to open, for the courage she’d need to step through them.
Most people don’t realize how much pressure young adults feel to “figure it all out.” The world shouts at them to chase success, but underneath, the heart is searching for something deeper. As parents, watching from the sidelines, you can’t map out every turn. But you can pray—for guidance, for the right mentors to come alongside, for passions to be uncovered and nurtured.
There’s another story—a father, watching his son bounce from job to job, worried he’d never settle. He prayed for patience, for the right opportunity, for his son to see his own gifts. And over time, that son found a role that just fit—the kind of work that brought both challenge and real joy. Looking back, the father realized that the journey, though long, had shaped his son in ways no one could’ve predicted.
Here’s something to remember—purpose isn’t always about your career. Sometimes it’s about serving others, building relationships, or finding meaning in the most unexpected places. If you’re a parent, you can pray for your child to discover what makes them come alive. Pray for courage—the courage to pursue their calling, and the trust to believe that every step, even the uncertain ones, really does matter.
